high.title: TSMC's Magnetic Effect Drives Science Parks to Near-Trillion Revenue, IC Industry Contributes Over 80%
high.summary: Taiwan's three major science parks achieved remarkable growth in the first two months of 2026, with combined revenue approaching NT$1 trillion at NT$992.1 billion (up 21.48% YoY). The integrated circuit industry alone generated NT$825.16 billion, representing over 83% of total park revenue and growing 23.36% YoY. Taiwan Economic Research Institute's Liu Pei-chen attributes this to TSMC's "magnetic effect," where the company's advanced process leadership translates into powerful growth momentum. With TSMC's 2026 capex raised to $52-56 billion, most spending flows to domestic science park facilities and R&D, creating this magnetic attraction. TSMC's 2nm process began volume production in late 2025 and is now ramping, while new facilities in Hsinchu Baoshan and Kaohsiung serve as global advanced process supply cores. This performance solidifies Taiwan's "silicon shield" and demonstrates the semiconductor sector's resilience amid global uncertainties.

high.title: Three Major Science Parks Write Double-Digit Growth Benefiting from Strong HPC and AI Demand
high.summary: Taiwan's science parks delivered exceptional performance in early 2026, with combined Jan-Feb revenue reaching NT$992.1 billion, up 21.48% YoY and just shy of the trillion-mark. NSC Vice Chairman Su Chen-kang attributed the growth to robust demand for high-performance computing (HPC), AI applications, optical communications, and electronic shelf labels (ESL). Southern Taiwan Science Park led with NT$492.97 billion revenue (up 22.25%), followed by Hsinchu at NT$301.88 billion (up 20.96%) and Central Taiwan at NT$197.26 billion (up 20.35%). The integrated circuit industry dominated with NT$825.16 billion revenue, representing over 80% of total park revenue and growing 23.36% YoY. Computer and peripheral products surged 59.44% to NT$42.5 billion, while biotech grew 25.45% to NT$9.04 billion. However, some traditional sectors faced headwinds, with optoelectronics declining 3.8% and communications down 6.89%.

high.title: Hon Hai Revenue Hits Record March High, Four Product Categories Show Strong Growth, AI Cabinet Shipments Hot
high.summary: Hon Hai reported record-high March revenue of NT$803.74 billion, marking the strongest March in company history. Q1 2026 consolidated revenue reached NT$2.129 trillion, the strongest first quarter ever, with all four major product categories showing robust growth. Month-over-month in March, computer terminal products and components benefited from low February base effects due to Chinese New Year and new product launches. Cloud and networking products grew strongly due to robust AI cloud product demand. Consumer smart products also showed strong growth from seasonal recovery and new product momentum. Year-over-year comparisons showed cloud/networking and consumer products with strong growth, driven by AI cloud demand and new product launches. Looking ahead to Q2, despite the traditional ICT industry seasonal slowdown and product transition periods, AI cabinet shipments maintain growth trends. Based on current visibility, Hon Hai expects Q2 operations to show both sequential and year-over-year growth, though global political and economic developments require continued monitoring.

high.title: Foreign and Domestic Investors Back Dark Horses in Strong Advance, Synnex Group and Mega Financial Gain Buying Interest
high.summary: Since the Middle East conflict erupted, foreign investors have withdrawn nearly NT$1 trillion (NT$983.6 billion) from Taiwan stocks, while domestic institutional investors mostly stood on the buy side during the same period. Screening for stocks that both foreign investors bought against the trend and domestic institutions accumulated over the past month, with combined net buying exceeding 4,500 shares and stock prices above monthly moving averages, 16 stocks emerged including Synnex Group (3702), Mega Financial (2886), Unimicron (3037), and Huaku Development (2548). Foreign and domestic investors combined bought over 91,000 shares of semiconductor distributor Synnex Group, attracted by stable dividend payments and advantages in AI server component supply plus flying car business ventures through subsidiaries. ABF substrate leader Unimicron, despite pulling back from its NT$594 historical high, saw institutions accumulate 16,000 shares during the pullback, with total buying reaching 190,000 shares year-to-date, anticipating cost-price increases in H1 and demand recovery in H2.

medium.title: AI Computing Demand Continues to Heat Up, Test Interface Four Leaders See Operational Explosion, Institutions Give Thumbs Up
medium.summary: Rising AI computing demand drives significant increases in HPC, ASIC, and advanced packaging test complexity, creating key growth opportunities for semiconductor test interface companies. Taiwan's test interface four leaders - Hung Ching (6515), Topco (6223), MPI (6510), and Chunghwa Precision Test Tech (6683) - show strengthening operational momentum. With AI, HPC, and ASIC orders boosting product portfolio upgrades and customer structure breakthroughs, institutions expect these four companies' operations to outperform last year.

medium.title: US-Iran War Pushes Up Oil Prices, Petrochemical Materials Surge, CPC and Formosa Plastics Respond
medium.summary: The US-Iran war has pushed up oil prices and petrochemical raw materials, leading to different response strategies between CPC and Formosa Petrochemical (6505). CPC urgently adjusted naphtha sources for its No. 4 naphtha cracker, running both crackers at full capacity. Conversely, Formosa Petrochemical suspended two of its three crackers due to raw material shortages. These different operational strategies will be reflected in Q2 performance, with institutions expecting the CPC petrochemical system to outperform Q1.

medium.title: Largan Revenue Writes Strongest Q1, iPhone 18 Expected to Feature Variable Aperture Lens for First Time
medium.summary: Largan Precision reported March revenue of NT$5.42 billion, up 17% MoM and 11% YoY, marking the second-highest March on record. Q1 revenue reached NT$15.54 billion, the strongest first quarter in history despite declining 9.7% QoQ. Chairman Lin En-ping indicated that due to seasonal new-old model transitions, April demand momentum may be weaker than March. Institutions expect the upcoming iPhone 18 series to feature variable aperture lenses for the first time, representing Apple's biggest upgrade in recent years.

medium.title: CCL Leader Lianmao March Revenue Up 29% MoM, Aggressively Promoting Ultra-Low Loss Substrate Materials
medium.summary: Copper clad laminate leader Lianmao reported record-high March revenue of NT$3.37 billion, up 29.11% MoM and 13.8% YoY. Q1 revenue of NT$9.14 billion also set a quarterly record, up 2.54% QoQ and 20.62% YoY. The company targets AI opportunities with new M9-grade Low CTE ultra-low loss substrate materials for AI data centers, having passed certification from major US AI GPU manufacturers and multiple PCB makers in H2 2025.

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Earnings Conference Season Shows Promise, TSMC, Delta Electronics Convening Successively, Expected to Catalyze Retaliatory Rebound
medium.summary: With Middle East warfare showing no signs of ending and Trump issuing another "hell will descend" ultimatum, market experts believe Taiwan stocks remain in consolidation in the near term. As earnings conference season builds momentum, bulls are eyeing TSMC's April 16 earnings call, which could lead the market in a new wave of retaliatory rebound if strong operational outlook is released. Key companies including Wistron, Delta Electronics, and Mega Financial will hold earnings calls throughout April.
